rationale: Added ch2: a dragBucket sort of 6 shapes (circle/triangle/square/rectangle) into 4 name buckets, extending ch1's single rotated-hexagon mcq into a batch judgment across all four taught shapes at once, with 2 items stated as pure side-count rules ("4 sides all the same length" / "2 long sides and 2 short sides") rather than pictures. New widget type for this lesson (dragBucket was previously unused here); new action (multi-item categorization vs single-item tap/mcq/matchPairs); new transfer demand (apply the invariance-under-turning rule from ch1 to 3 more shapes simultaneously while also discriminating square vs rectangle by side count, which k2/i2 only ever test one at a time). All 6 item->bucket assignments verified by hand against the lesson's own taught definitions (c1: circle round, triangle 3 sides, square 4 equal sides; c2: rectangle 2 long+2 short). Gates: schema clean, pedagogy clean, session267 course test passes (ch1 untouched, still mcq).
reopenCondition: Lesson or course source bytes change (review basis hash drift), or ch2's bucket assignments are found inconsistent with c1/c2/k2/i2's stated side-count rules.

rationale: Added ch2: a dragBucket sort of 6 shapes where 4 keep their name through a turn/flip/even-resize (matching c1's rule) and 2 are deliberately stretched or squeezed UNEVENLY so the rule's precondition breaks and the name genuinely changes (square stretched wide -> rectangle; rectangle squeezed narrow -> square). This is a new misconception target not tested anywhere in the lesson: every existing item (i1/k1/i2/k2/k3/ch1) only ever shows transformations that preserve the name, so a learner is never asked to recognize the boundary of the invariance rule. Both boundary cases verified against the lesson's own definitions (square = 4 equal sides, rectangle = 2 long + 2 short) with no contradiction of c1's 'turn/flip/resize keeps the name' claim (that claim is about even transformations; the new items explicitly narrate an UNEVEN stretch/squeeze as the differentiator). Gates: schema clean, pedagogy clean, session267 course test passes (ch1 untouched, still matchPairs).
reopenCondition: Lesson or course source bytes change (review basis hash drift), or ch2's uneven-stretch items are found to contradict c1's turn/flip/resize invariance claim rather than narrating a genuinely different (non-uniform) transformation.

rationale: Added ch2: a tapDiagram selectAll item ("tap every friend that is NOT above the barn", 3 of 4 hotspots correct) — the first selectAll/negation item in the lesson (i1/k1/i2 are all selectOne) and the first hands-on item to include in-front/behind alongside above/below/beside (currently front/behind only appear in abstract mcq form in k2/k3, never in a spatial task). Targets a genuinely new misconception: over-generalizing k2's 'above's opposite is below' into 'NOT above means only below', when NOT above is the larger set {below, beside, behind}. Verified: cat is the only friend above the barn, so the correct selection is exactly {dog, frog, mouse} (3 of 4); missFeedback is written to name the undercount case (tapping only 'dog') as the primary anticipated error. Gates: schema clean, pedagogy clean, session267 course test passes (ch1 untouched, still dragBucket).
reopenCondition: Lesson or course source bytes change (review basis hash drift), or ch2's correct-set {dog, frog, mouse} is found inconsistent with the barn scene as narrated in its own prompt.

rationale: Added ch2: a 5-bucket dragBucket sort (sphere/cube/cylinder/cone/"flat, not a solid") that folds in 2 flat-paper distractors (a paper circle, a whiteboard square) alongside 5 genuine solids. Picks up the flat-vs-solid contrast the lesson's own c1 figure is literally named for ("flat-vs-solid", shared with ks-01-01) but that no existing item tests explicitly — every current item (i1/k1/i2/k2/k3/ch1) presents only solids, so a learner is never asked to first decide whether something IS a solid at all versus reusing a flat-shape word (circle/square) for it. New widget type for this lesson (dragBucket was unused here) and a genuine cross-lesson transfer demand back to ks-01-01's flat-shape vocabulary. All 7 item assignments verified against the lesson's own definitions (c1: ball=sphere, dice=cube, can=cylinder, hat=cone) with the 2 flat items excluded from all 4 solid buckets since a paper cutout has no depth. Gates: schema clean, pedagogy clean, session267 course test passes (ch1 untouched, still mcq).
reopenCondition: Lesson or course source bytes change (review basis hash drift), or ch2's flat-vs-solid item assignments are found inconsistent with c1/c2's own solid definitions.

rationale: Added ch2: a numeric-entry item ("2 triangles build 1 square; how many triangles for 4 squares?", answer 8) with 3 anticipated wrong counts (4, 6, 2) each diagnosing a distinct miscount. This is the first typed-numeric item in the lesson (current surfaces are tapDiagram/mcq/matchPairs/dragBucket, i.e. every existing item is single-instance picture/pairing recognition) and the first to require SCALING a composition fact across multiple copies rather than recognizing one built shape. Directly precedented by g0Variants.ts's own shapeComposeMcq generator, whose second (currently unauthored-in-this-lesson) branch already validates the identical 'N squares need N groups of 2 triangles' relationship for this exact concept tag/course — so the underlying math pattern was already sound in this codebase, just never assessed in ks-02-03's authored content. Verified by hand: 4 squares x 2 triangles/square = 8; all 3 traps (4, 6, 2) are < 8 and mutually distinct. Gates: schema clean, pedagogy clean (numeric challenge with >=2 commonErrors satisfied), session267 course test passes (ch1 untouched, still dragBucket).
reopenCondition: Lesson or course source bytes change (review basis hash drift), or ch2's answer is found not to equal 4 times the lesson's own 2-triangles-per-square composition fact.

rationale: Added ch2: a 4-bucket dragBucket sort (Heavier/Lighter/Holds more/Holds less) mixing 4 weight clues and 3 capacity clues, the first task in the lesson requiring the learner to first identify WHICH property a clue is about before judging its direction. Every existing item is single-dimension by construction (i1/k1/k2 are pure weight, i2/k3 are pure capacity, ch1's dragBucket sorts weight clues only into heavier/lighter/same) — none ever mixes the two properties, so discriminating a weight clue from a capacity clue was never actually exercised. Also reinforces the size-trick misconception (k1) with a fresh object pair (block/stone) and extends the pouring-overflow representation (i2) to the 'holds less' direction via 2 new overflow narratives (teacup/teapot, small cup/jug), which currently only appears via bare size intuition (k3). All 7 item conclusions verified by hand against the lesson's own rules (seesaw down=heavier/up=lighter from c1/k2; leftover room after pouring=holds more from i2; by symmetry, an early overflow=holds less). Gates: schema clean, pedagogy clean, session267 course test passes (ch1 untouched, still dragBucket).
reopenCondition: Lesson or course source bytes change (review basis hash drift), or ch2's weight/capacity classification for any item is found inconsistent with c1/c2/i2's own seesaw-and-pouring rules.
